et museum.explanation: "Et museum" means "a museum". To say you are at the museum, use "på" (at): "Jeg er på museet" (I am at the museum).

et mysterium.explanation: "Et mysterium" means "a mystery". To say someone solves a mystery, use "at løse" (to solve): "Detektiven løser mysteriet" (The detective solves the mystery).

et mål.explanation: "Et mål" means "a goal". To say someone scored in a sport, say: "Han scorede to mål" (He scored two goals).

et målebånd.explanation: "Et målebånd" means "a tape measure". It is built from "at måle" (to measure) and "et bånd" (a band). The word "måle" also starts "et målebæger" (a measuring cup).

et målebæger.explanation: "Et målebæger" means "a measuring cup". It is built from "at måle" (to measure) and "et bæger" (a cup). The word "måle" also starts "et målebånd" (a tape measure).

et måltid.explanation: "Et måltid" means "a meal". To say a meal is hot, use "varmt" (hot): "Vi spiser et varmt måltid hver aften" (We eat a hot meal every evening). To talk about the food itself, use "mad" (food): "Maden er god" (The food is good).

et månedskort.explanation: "Et månedskort" means "a monthly pass". It is built from "måned" (month) and "kort" (card). The word "kort" also means a card in "et kreditkort" (a credit card).

et mærke.explanation: "Et mærke" means "a brand / mark". To ask what brand something is, say: "Hvilket mærke er din telefon?" (What brand is your phone?). To talk about a mark on a surface, say: "et mærke på væggen" (a mark on the wall).

et møbel.explanation: "Et møbel" means "a piece of furniture". To talk about furniture as a whole, use the plural "møbler" (furniture): "Vi køber nye møbler" (We are buying new furniture).

et møde.explanation: "Et møde" means "a meeting". To say people hold a meeting, use "at holde" (to hold): "Vi holder et møde i morgen" (We are holding a meeting tomorrow). The verb "at møde" (to meet) is spelled the same: "Jeg møder dig i morgen" (I meet you tomorrow).

et mødelokale.explanation: "Et mødelokale" means "a meeting room". It is built from "et møde" (a meeting) and "et lokale" (a room in a building). To talk about a room in a home or a hotel, use "et værelse" (a room): "Jeg sover på mit værelse" (I sleep in my room).

et mønster.explanation: "Et mønster" means "a pattern". To talk about a design on cloth, say: "et mønster med blomster" (a pattern with flowers). To talk about a pattern in what someone does, say: "et mønster i hans opførsel" (a pattern in his behavior).

mad.explanation: "Mad" means "food". To say someone cooks, use "at lave mad" (to cook): "Jeg laver mad hver dag" (I cook every day). Do not mix it up with "en mad", which means a sandwich: "en mad med ost" (a sandwich with cheese).

madlavning.explanation: "Madlavning" means "cooking". It is built from "mad" (food) and "at lave" (to make). To say someone is cooking, use "at lave mad": "Han laver mad" (He is cooking).

madpapir.explanation: "Et madpapir" means "sandwich paper". It is built from "en mad" (a sandwich) and "et papir" (a paper). The word "papir" also ends "toiletpapir" (toilet paper).

madspild.explanation: "Madspild" means "food waste". It is built from "mad" (food) and "et spild" (waste). To say you want to avoid it, use "at undgå" (to avoid): "Vi vil gerne undgå madspild" (We would like to avoid food waste).

mager.explanation: "Mager" means "lean". To describe a person, it means "skinny": "Han er meget mager" (He is very skinny).

magi.explanation: "Magi" means "magic". To say a moment feels special, say: "Der er magi i luften" (There is magic in the air).

magisk.explanation: "Magisk" means "magical". It is the adjective for "magi" (magic). To say a moment was wonderful, say: "Det var magisk!" (It was magical!)

magtfuld.explanation: "Magtfuld" means "powerful". It is built from "en magt" (power) and "fuld" (full). To say someone has strong muscles, use "stærk" (strong): "Bokseren er meget stærk" (The boxer is very strong).

maj.explanation: "Maj" means "May". In the middle of a sentence, write the month as "maj", not "Maj": "Det er varmt i maj" (It is warm in May).

majs.explanation: "Majs" means "corn", as in the vegetable. To talk about eating it, use no article: "Jeg spiser majs" (I eat corn). To point to one ear of corn, use "en majskolbe": "Jeg spiser en majskolbe" (I eat an ear of corn).

makeup.explanation: "Makeup" means "makeup". To say someone puts on makeup, use "at tage ... på" (to put on): "Hun tager makeup på" (She puts on makeup).

maksimal.explanation: "Maksimal" means "maximum". Danish spells it with "ks", not "x": "maksimal". To say "at most", use "maksimalt": "Der er plads til maksimalt ti personer" (There is room for at most ten people).

malerisk.explanation: "Malerisk" means "picturesque". It comes from "at male" (to paint). The adjective ending "-isk" also appears in "magisk" (magical) and "praktisk" (practical).
